ri_jungle_pond.blurb: Jungle Pond is a bouldering ledge in the forest east of Beach Pond, in the Rhode Island woods near the Connecticut line. The wall runs at least 75 to 100 feet, and the cleanest climbing sits in its middle stretch. Its 20 problems cover a wide spread: a handful of easy lines, a solid core around V2 to V4, and a few hard problems up to about V6. The ledge looks out to the west, and there is room left for more lines further south. Expect dense woods, a short climber's trail from the road, and poison ivy in season. A good stop on a day of exploring the pond's boulders.

ri_black_point.blurb: Black Point is a small seaside bouldering spot on the Narragansett coast, one of several short shoreline problems strung along Route 1 South. Twenty boulder problems range from easy warm-ups at V0 through a good middle band of V2 to V4, then a few hard test pieces reaching V8. The walk from the car is very short and the views over the water are excellent. Climbers note strong friction in winter, while summer brings a steady sea breeze. Some blocks sit beside a tidal pool, so watch the water. It pairs well with a beach day when you want a quick session.

sc_main_wall.blurb: The Main Wall is the biggest cliff face at Big Rock Mountain near Pickens, and it holds the densest cluster of routes in the area, some of them the best here. It leans toward trad with a handful of bolted lines, and some routes can be strung into multipitch. Grades start near 5.7 and cluster in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, topping out around 5.12. The granite faces mostly south and shakes off rain quickly, which makes it a good cool-season choice. Warm months bring bugs and overgrowth. All trails from the main lot reach it in about the same walking distance.
sc_main_wall.parking_note: Use the gravel lot on Big Rock Lake Road. If it is full, extra cars can park where Nine Times Road meets Preston McDaniel Road.

sc_x_wall.blurb: X-Wall is a well-featured southeast-facing wall at Big Rock Mountain near Pickens. About twenty routes mix trad with a few bolted lines and one top-rope, with grades running from the mid 5.6 range into the low 5.11s and the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10. Several lines stay damp for days after heavy rain, so give it time to dry. The sunny exposure makes it a pleasant cool-season wall, and it is friendly to climbers working through the moderates. The trail to it is the right-hand branch out of the main lot, and a landing at the base has a pair of 5.8s.
sc_x_wall.parking_note: Use the gravel lot on Big Rock Lake Road. If it is full, extra cars can park where Nine Times Road meets Preston McDaniel Road.
sc_x_wall.approach: Take the right-hand fork of the trail from the main lot to the cliff.

_expect.name: Main Wall Left of Center Buttress

sc_main_wall_left_of_center_buttress.blurb: This stretch of the Pumpkintown cliff in Table Rock State Park lies west of the big, obvious buttress near the middle of the wall. It has twenty routes, mostly trad with six bolted lines, and the face climbing is the draw, often following water grooves. Grades run from one 5.9 through a thick band of 5.10 and 5.11 to a couple of 5.12s, so it suits confident leaders more than beginners. Many routes are two pitches. Reaching the wall means a trail along the base of the cliff, and getting around the buttress takes a rugged or exposed move or a fixed rope.

sd_weather_watchers_wall.blurb: Weather Watchers Wall is the principal cliff of Raspberry Rocks, a quiet granite ridge in the Needles of Rushmore near Keystone. It is among the steepest and longest walls in the Black Hills, with corners, aretes, cracks and a big tiered roof near the center. Most of its 28 routes are trad, with a few bolted and one top-rope line, and grades span 5.8 up to the 5.12s with plenty in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. The wall looks west-northwest, so mornings are shady and the sun arrives in the afternoon. Reaching it means a faint trail and a talus and boulder scramble below the face.

sd_asylum_the.blurb: The Asylum is a sport wall within the Mohican section of Spearfish Canyon in the Black Hills. Its 27 bolted routes are hard and technical, running from about 5.10 into the 5.13s, with the heart of it in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The style is unusual for the canyon, with steep, demanding slab and little forgiveness, so expect to work routes rather than onsight them. It is a place for strong, patient climbers, not for people looking for an easy warm-up day. The walk in follows the first trail from the parking area, bearing left beyond the Head Shop Wall.

sd_holy_hanna.blurb: Holy Hanna is the main sport crag of the Hanna Road Crags in Spearfish Canyon, found up the hillside above the road and campground. Its 25 limestone routes are mostly moderate-to-hard, with one 5.7, a big group at 5.10 and 5.11, and several at 5.12. The routes are known for steep rock with big holds, and the 5.10s are especially well regarded. The crag has two walls; the left one faces north and stays shaded in the morning, while the right side gets shade later in the day. The hike from the road is a rough path through the woods.
